episodes.title: OpenClaw Step by Step: Setup Your AI Assistant 100% Locally (Telegram + Ollama)
episodes.summary: This episode explores OpenClaw's multi-channel communication capabilities, covering Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp integrations. The host demonstrates configuring each channel, explains the differences in how they handle messages and reactions, and shows how agents can operate across multiple channels simultaneously. Platform-specific features like Discord threads and Telegram reactions are highlighted.
keyTakeaways: OpenClaw supports Telegram, Discord, and WhatsApp as communication channels
Each channel has unique features - Discord has threads, Telegram has reactions
Agents can operate across multiple channels with the same underlying capabilities
Channel configuration determines how the agent responds (mentions vs all messages)
Different formatting rules apply per platform (no tables in Discord, no headers in WhatsApp)
episodes.priscyllaTake: Eric uses Telegram as his primary channel, but knowing Discord and WhatsApp are available gives flexibility. For his DJ business, Telegram works great for direct communication, while Discord could be useful for community building around his AI artists. I need to remember platform formatting rules - no markdown tables in Discord!

expandedTakeaways.title: Channel-Specific Features
expandedTakeaways.detail: Leverage each platform's strengths: Discord for communities, Telegram for direct messaging, WhatsApp for broad reach.

expandedTakeaways.title: Configuration Options
expandedTakeaways.detail: Channels can be configured to require mentions or respond to all messages, controlling agent visibility.

expandedTakeaways.title: Formatting Adaptation
expandedTakeaways.detail: Agents automatically adapt output formatting to match platform capabilities and limitations.

expandedTakeaways.title: Cross-Channel Consistency
expandedTakeaways.detail: Core capabilities remain consistent across channels, providing unified experience regardless of platform.

episodes.title: My Multi-Agent Team with OpenClaw
episodes.summary: This episode explores patterns for multi-agent collaboration in OpenClaw. The host demonstrates how agents can delegate tasks to subagents, share results, and coordinate on complex workflows. Patterns include manager-worker relationships, peer-to-peer collaboration, and pipeline processing. Communication mechanisms and result aggregation are also covered.
keyTakeaways: Multi-agent patterns enable complex task decomposition
Manager-worker pattern delegates subtasks to specialized subagents
Pipeline pattern chains agents for sequential processing
Results auto-announce back to parent agents when complete
Clear task definitions prevent confusion and duplication
episodes.priscyllaTake: Multi-agent collaboration is powerful for Eric's music label - one agent could research playlists while another generates artist content while a third handles social media. I'm currently a single subagent, but complex workflows could involve multiple subagents working in parallel on different aspects of a release campaign.

expandedTakeaways.title: Task Decomposition
expandedTakeaways.detail: Break complex tasks into smaller, independent subtasks that can be parallelized across agents.

expandedTakeaways.title: Communication Patterns
expandedTakeaways.detail: Push-based completion eliminates polling overhead and enables efficient result aggregation.

expandedTakeaways.title: Specialization Benefits
expandedTakeaways.detail: Different agents can specialize in different domains (research, writing, analysis) for better results.

expandedTakeaways.title: Coordination Overhead
expandedTakeaways.detail: Balance parallelization benefits against coordination costs - not all tasks benefit from multi-agent approaches.
